name: Token Predictability Ranking
description: Evaluates the likelihood of each word being explicitly predicted by an AI model based on its preceding context. Utilizing principles from GLTR (Giant Language Model Test Room, Gehrmann et al., 2019) and zero-shot probability curvature (Mitchell et al., 2023), this method maps the 'predictability contour' of a text. Generative AI models function by continually selecting the statistically most probable next token. Consequently, AI-authored text overwhelmingly consists of 'Top-10' predictability words. Human writers, however, frequently and unpredictably select statistically suboptimal (low-probability) words driven by personal vocabulary, emotion, or stylistic idiosyncrasies.
mechanism: The algorithm processes the input text sequentially through an N-gram or lightweight proxy language model to calculate the conditional probability of every token given its preceding context. Each word is ranked based on its predictability: 'Top-10' (highly predictable), 'Top-100' (moderately predictable), or 'Tail' (unpredictable). The system analyzes the text's probability curvature—the density and distribution of these ranks. A text dominated almost entirely by 'Top-10' tokens with a smooth probability contour is highly indicative of auto-regressive machine generation. A text featuring frequent spikes into 'Tail' token territory signifies human authorship.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing short to medium-length documents (news articles, reports, student essays) by visualizing and quantifying the exact artificial 'smoothness' of the vocabulary choices.
strengths:
• Can often detect AI generation even when the text has been subjected to basic paraphrasing, as the underlying statistical bias toward predictable words remains strong.
• Zero-shot detection capability; does not require training a separate classification model, relying instead on pure statistical distributions.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives on human texts that use highly standardized, formulaic language (e.g., weather reports, legal boilerplate, or simple instructional manuals where 'predictable' words are mandatory).
• Requires a reference language model or robust N-gram database to accurately estimate token probabilities.
parameters:
Analysis: Conditional Token Probability Ranking
Metric: Density of Top-K vs. Tail Token Selection
Output: 0-100 Auto-Regressive Predictability Score
accuracy: High — 82-88% accuracy. Widely considered one of the most reliable and academically robust baseline mechanisms for detecting unedited machine-generated text.

references.title: Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL.
Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.

source: Gehrmann, S. et al. (2019). GLTR: Statistical Detection and Visualization of Generated Text. ACL.; Mitchell, E. et al. (2023). DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature. ICML.
